title: bug: withPolicyRiskLeg SILENTLY DROPS the risk leg when its build refuses, so the ordinary journey records no policy-risk authority at all and nothing says so
description:
SUCCESSOR TO task-510340a346c24615a2177c2db9a85782, filed by worker-da0aeedb on 2026-09-12 from that row's step 7. That row was required to file this rather than leave it in a sentence. It fixed the CONSUMER (automatic preview now reads the goal's replay-verified planning-run tier); this row is the UPSTREAM fail-open it deliberately did not take, because changing approval activation touches EVERY action and not just preview.

THE FAIL-OPEN, measured by me at HEAD f6e97a6b with an out-of-tree probe over a completed `journeyWorld("SUBMITTED")`:

    store.enumerateAggregateIdsByPrefix("policy-risk:sha256:")  ->  []          (ZERO records)
    readPolicyRisk(store, project-1, OPERATOR, "plan.approve")  ->  POLICY_RISK_RECORD_MISSING @ DAEMON_POLICY_RISK, tier null, truthClass UNKNOWN
    readPolicyRisk(store, project-1, OPERATOR, "preview.decide") -> POLICY_RISK_RECORD_MISSING @ DAEMON_POLICY_RISK, tier null, truthClass UNKNOWN
    readCurrentActiveGraph(store, project-1)                    ->  ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT @ ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION

THE MECHANISM, three files, each verified in source:
1. `apps/daemon/src/planning/policy-risk-leg.ts:141` -- `withPolicyRiskLeg` ends
   `return built.ok ? [...legs, built.leg] : legs`. It DROPS the leg on refusal and tells NOBODY:
   no code, no log, no counter, no refusal reaching any caller.
2. `policy-risk-leg.ts:72-74` -- `buildPolicyRiskLeg` refuses POLICY_RISK_SUBJECT_UNAVAILABLE when
   `input.subject === null` or `subjectRevision < 1`.
3. `apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-activation.ts` Path B has no graph-revision activation leg.
   It reads `readCurrentActiveGraph` and supplies `subject: null` when that answers
   ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT -- which IS the ordinary journey. So the leg never runs on any real project.

WHY THE SILENCE IS THE DEFECT AND NOT THE DROP. policy-risk-leg.ts:118-121 argues the refusal is silent on purpose: "a human approving a plan must not be blocked by the absence of a risk tier ... those are reasons to record NO risk authority, not reasons to refuse the approval." That reasoning is sound and this row should NOT turn it into an approval refusal. What is not sound is that the intended state ("no risk authority was recorded, and here is which of the five conditions caused it") is INDISTINGUISHABLE from "the writer ran and everything was fine". A whole class of consumer bugs hides in that gap -- task-510340a3 is one instance, found by an external review and not by any gate, and the suite stayed green for weeks because the tests inserted the missing record by hand.

WHAT THIS ROW LIKELY OWES, for the architect to shape rather than accept as given:
- Make the DROP OBSERVABLE without making it blocking. The refusal already carries a code and a
  layer (`policyRiskRefusal`); today they are discarded. Surfacing them -- a returned diagnosis
  alongside the legs, or a durable "risk authority not recorded, reason X" marker -- is the
  smallest change that makes the state legible to an operator and assertable by a test.
- DECIDE whether Path B should activate a graph revision at all. `gates-unattended-fixtures.ts`
  used to FABRICATE one after approval precisely because the journey leaves none behind, with a
  comment saying so; task-510340a3 deleted that fabrication. If plan approval is supposed to leave
  an active graph revision, that is a real product gap and its blast radius is every consumer of
  `readCurrentActiveGraph`, not just the risk reader.
- COUNT THE OTHER CONSUMERS before choosing. `readPolicyRisk` is reached through
  `resolvePolicyFact`, which `bootstrap-policy-services.ts:173` still uses for `validatePolicy`'s
  caller-named action. Automatic preview NO LONGER reads it (task-510340a3 moved that to
  `preview/preview-risk-fact.ts`), so measure who is left rather than assuming.

VERIFY BEFORE PLANNING, because this description is stale by default:
    grep -n 'built.ok ? ' apps/daemon/src/planning/policy-risk-leg.ts
    grep -rn 'withPolicyRiskLeg' apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v test
    grep -rn 'readCurrentActiveGraph' apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v test
    grep -rn 'resolvePolicyFact' apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v test
Read task-510340a3's completionSummary and comment-891b32d34a104c4cb076cb77ca0660bc first: it records the measurement, the reachability limits of the journey world, and why the consumer-side fix was taken.

NOT A DUPLICATE: I searched epic-af14d735 for an owner of this capability before filing. The six related rows (task-a47301ee, task-d56a0cc5, task-b8571cfe, task-24b68b05, task-6cbcf5ff, task-510340a3) are all DONE or this row's parent, and none owns the upstream writer's silence.
definitionOfDone: The ordinary journey's failure to record policy-risk authority is OBSERVABLE: a test drives the production approval path over a real journey world, asserts zero policy-risk records, and asserts the specific refusal CODE and LAYER that explain why (today POLICY_RISK_SUBJECT_UNAVAILABLE at the writer, from ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT @ ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION upstream). Asserting only 'no record exists' is the vacuous form this row exists to end.

A human plan approval is still NEVER blocked by the absence of a risk tier, an unauthenticated transport, or an unreadable subject. Assert it: an approval whose risk leg is refused still COMMITS, and the arm names the refusal reason it tolerated.

Every remaining consumer of readPolicyRisk / resolvePolicyFact is enumerated by grep at plan time and named, with its behaviour on the no-record state asserted or explicitly out of scope. Automatic preview is NOT one of them any more (task-510340a3 moved it to preview/preview-risk-fact.ts) - confirm that by grep rather than inheriting it.

If the row concludes that plan approval SHOULD leave an active graph revision, that change is either made with every readCurrentActiveGraph consumer named in the plan's owned paths, or split out as its own row with the gap measured consumer by consumer. It is not half-made.
Non-vacuity: re-introduce the silent drop (or re-null the subject) and confirm the observability arm reds with the specific code and layer, not merely with a count change. Quote the red.

pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with the `Test Files N passed (N)` count line quoted. If a foreign red is present, record the path-attributed baseline per global rail 3 and disclose it verbatim.

implementationPlan.description: REPRODUCE THE CEILING BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING - read only, and this is the step the last plan did not have. Re-run worker-a1cf5270's probe (preserved in comment-612abc32): a logging Proxy over `store.commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs`, methods bound to the real store, driving `approvePlan` over the production `boundWorld -> committedRevision -> approveGate1 -> submit` path. CONFIRM the ordinary journey's plan approval commits EXACTLY 8 legs and that `MAX_DECISION_LEGS` in `packages/store/src/decision-legs-contracts.ts` is still 8. Record the leg list verbatim - it is the baseline step 3 must prove unchanged. Then re-pin the seam: `policy-risk-leg.ts:141` is still `return built.ok ? [...legs, built.leg] : legs;`; `withPolicyRiskLeg` still has exactly TWO production callers (`approval-activation.ts`, `graph-activation-service.ts`), both taking `context: HandlerContext`; `approval-record-facts.test.ts:419` still asserts exactly ONE `commitAcceptedLegs(` in approval-activation.ts's source text. IF THE LEG COUNT IS NOT 8, STOP and report_blocked - the budget moved, and every design decision below was made against 8.

MAKE THE REFUSAL LEAVE THE HELPER, AND ADD NO LEG. In `policy-risk-leg.ts`, change `withPolicyRiskLeg` to return the legs AND the refusal that was discarded at :141 - `{ legs, refusal }`, where `refusal` is the existing `policyRiskRefusal` value (carrying its code and layer) or null when the leg built. THE LEG ARRAY IS NEVER WIDENED: on refusal it returns the caller's legs unchanged, exactly as today. This is the whole reason the design changed - there is zero spare leg budget on this path. Add the observation sink in the same file: a module-level default that emits the code and layer (a log line, in the house's existing style) so production is legible WITHOUT any composition-root wiring, overridable per-call. In `bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger-vocabulary.ts`, add ONE optional member to `HandlerContext` for that override, following the convention the interface already uses at :239-251 for `compiledContractBinding?`, `humanReview?` and `receipts?` - assembled outside decoded command bytes, absent meaning 'nothing supplied'. Absent must fall back to the default sink, never to silence: a test that forgets to inject must still not resurrect the bug this row exists to fix.

WIRE `approval-activation.ts`, AND PROVE THE LEG COUNT DID NOT MOVE. Consume the new `{legs, refusal}` shape in `activateInitialGraphDecision` (the caller at :118) and hand the refusal to the sink, passing `context`'s optional observer when present. CARRY FORWARD worker-a1cf5270's step-3 fix, which stands on its own merits and is the one piece of the previous attempt that survives: the `riskLegs.length === 0` slot-fence test must keep meaning 'no RISK leg was produced' and the fence's behaviour must be byte-identical to today's for every input. Note the previous attempt found this at :202 where the old plan said :200 - use the line the file actually has. LEAVE THE COMMIT SHAPE ALONE: one `commitAcceptedLegs(` call (pinned by `approval-record-facts.test.ts:419`), `extraLegs`/`sourceFences`/`replayLeg` in their existing order, the burn last. Then RE-RUN THE STEP-1 PROBE and confirm the leg list is byte-identical to the baseline - same 8 aggregates, same order. A diagnosis that costs a leg is the failure this replan exists to avoid, and it must be disproved by measurement rather than by reading the diff.

WIRE `graph-activation-service.ts`, the second and quieter caller (`activateApprovedGraph` at :161, its decision helper at :130). Consume the same `{legs, refusal}` shape and hand the refusal to the same sink. This caller derives its subject from the TRANSITION rather than from `readCurrentActiveGraph` (see its comment at :245), so its leg normally BUILDS and the refusal is its rare path - but it must not keep a silent drop after this row. Confirm its `extraLegs` composition is unchanged and that it still rides ONE `commitAcceptedLegs`. Do NOT unify the two callers' subject derivation: :245 explains deliberately why they differ, and that question belongs to task-c055f6af6e63412c905d02a3ac657a57. Check this path's own leg count too - the revision leg is ALWAYS present here per :240-243, so its budget is not the same as approval's and a refusal-path change must not push it over 8 either.

STATE THE PROPERTY AND THE COMPROMISE IN THE HEADER. `policy-risk-leg.ts:118-121` argues the refusal is silent on purpose, and its REASONING IS CORRECT - a human approving a plan must not be blocked by a missing tier, an unauthenticated transport, or an unreadable subject. Keep that. Rewrite the claim of SILENCE: the approval is still never blocked, and the omission is now reported with the code and layer that caused it, so 'no risk authority was recorded, for reason X' is distinguishable from 'the writer ran and everything was fine' - the gap that let task-510340a3's consumer bug hide behind a green suite for weeks. THEN SAY PLAINLY WHY THE REPORT IS OFF-LEDGER RATHER THAN DURABLE, naming the cause: this decision path already commits exactly 8 legs against a `MAX_DECISION_LEGS` of 8, and `packages/store/src/decision-legs-contracts.ts:3-8` documents that bound as deliberate - every leg costs another version probe and receipt inside one write transaction. A durable marker would be a 9th leg and would turn a fail-OPEN approval into a hard throw. Write that as the measured reason it is, so the next reader does not re-derive the probe from scratch or conclude nobody bothered to persist it. Also enumerate the consumers of the no-record state: `resolvePolicyFact` -> `readPolicyRisk` has ONE production caller (`bootstrap-policy-services.ts:173`), and automatic preview is NOT among them any more - name preview's departure explicitly so the stale belief is not re-inherited.

THE ARMS, in a new `policy-risk-observability.test.ts`, all driving PRODUCTION paths. (a) DoD 1: drive the real approval over a real `journeyWorld("SUBMITTED")` with a recorder injected through the `HandlerContext` member, assert `enumerateAggregateIdsByPrefix("policy-risk:sha256:")` is still EMPTY, and assert the recorder captured POLICY_RISK_SUBJECT_UNAVAILABLE WITH ITS LAYER. Asserting only that no record exists is the vacuous form this row exists to end. (b) DoD 2, fail-open preserved: the approval whose risk leg was refused still COMMITS, and the arm names the refusal reason it tolerated. Cover at least TWO distinct causes so the sink is not hard-coded to one - SUBJECT_UNAVAILABLE from the journey plus one of ACTOR_NOT_HUMAN or TIER_MISSING driven by input. (c) THE LEG-COUNT REGRESSION ARM, the most valuable thing to come out of this replan: pin that the ordinary journey's plan approval commits EXACTLY 8 legs, naming them. This is what makes the next design that wants a 9th leg fail in a test instead of at step 4 of a plan, which is how this row lost an attempt. (d) THE SLOT-FENCE GUARD: an approval that takes the slot fence today still takes it, one that does not still does not - assert the fence leg's presence directly. (e) DoD 3: `bootstrap-policy-services.ts`'s `validatePolicy` path still answers its UNKNOWN truthClass on the no-record state, pinned so it stays that way.

VERIFY, ONCE, AT THE END. First DoD 5's non-vacuity: restore `policy-risk-leg.ts` to the silent `built.ok ? [...legs, built.leg] : legs`, re-run arm (a), and QUOTE THE RED showing it fails on the missing CODE AND LAYER - not merely on a count change. Separately confirm arm (c) is non-vacuous by adding a throwaway 9th leg and quoting the STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED it produces, then removing it. Restore, then run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and quote the `Test Files N passed (N)` line with the exit code; an exit code alone is not evidence. The last attempt measured 619 passed (619) at HEAD bae9758d on a clean tree - compare against a fresh baseline, not that figure, since peers land continuously. This row adds NO runtime command kind, so epic rails 1 and 2 do not fire: no `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` leg and no digest-mirror census is owed. Legitimate neighbours are `approval-record-facts.test.ts`, `approval-activation.test.ts`, `graph-activation-service.test.ts` and the criterion-evidence suites the last attempt reddened; a red elsewhere on this shared branch is more likely a peer's bytes - attribute before fixing.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, ONCE, AT THE END - read the diff as someone trying to make an approval silently lose its risk authority again, and as someone trying to blow the leg budget. Answer each with a file:line. (1) Does ANY refusal exit in `buildPolicyRiskLeg` - all six, including `buildPolicyRiskRecord`'s `!record.ok` - still return without reaching the sink? Walk every one. (2) Does the returned leg array EVER grow on a refusal path, in either caller? This is the failure that cost the previous attempt; prove it from the step-3 probe output, not from reading. (3) Is the slot fence's behaviour identical to before for every input, now that the caller reads a refusal rather than a length? (4) Does `approval-activation.ts` still contain EXACTLY ONE `commitAcceptedLegs(` occurrence so `approval-record-facts.test.ts:419` holds? (5) When the optional `HandlerContext` member is ABSENT, does the default sink still report - or did an `undefined` check accidentally restore the silence this row exists to end? (6) Does the header state, as a measured fact with the file and line, WHY the report is off-ledger? A 'yes' with no file:line is not an answer.

comments.content:
MEASUREMENT THAT BLOCKS THE PLAN'S CHOSEN DESIGN — worker-a1cf5270, step 3, branch moe/work-2026-09-11.

THE ORDINARY JOURNEY'S PLAN APPROVAL ALREADY RIDES EXACTLY 8 LEGS, AND 8 IS THE STORE'S HARD MAXIMUM. Adding the absence marker makes it 9 and the store THROWS.

Measured with a logging Proxy over `store.commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs` (methods bound to the real store), driving `approvePlan` over the production `boundWorld -> committedRevision -> approveGate1 -> submit` path — the same path `journeyWorld` takes:

    PROBE4 legs 9 ["goal-1","moe-budget-ledger/1|aggregate|9:pr","policy-risk-absent:sha256:e008473e","run-1","planning-authority/run-1","project-1-policy","policy-run-evaluation:run-1","active-graph-slot:project-1","moe.session-authority.v1/replay/ad"]
    PROBE4 THREW DurableStoreError: STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: legs cannot exceed 8 elements

Remove leg 3 (my marker) and it is exactly 8. The budget on `activateInitialGraphWithApprovalReplay` is fixed: 1 primary (goal) + 1 GENESIS budget root + N risk legs + 5 source fences (`approval-intent-source-fences.ts:59-65` — run, planning-authority, project-policy, run-policy, active-graph-slot) + 1 replay marker. `slotFenceLegs` is already `[]` on this path because `approvalSourceFences !== undefined`. THE CONSEQUENCE THE PLAN DID NOT ANTICIPATE: the silent drop is load-bearing in a SECOND and much harder way than planningNotes.codebaseInsights found. A risk leg that actually BUILT on this path would already throw today. The path has ZERO spare leg budget.

This inverts exactly the property DoD 2 pins: a marker leg turns a fail-OPEN approval into a hard STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED throw. Blast radius measured on the full daemon suite with the marker in place: 60+ failures across gates-compose-journey, bootstrap-durability, criterion-approval/command/integrated/read/run — every suite whose fixture approves a plan.

comments.author: architect-76be3b8c
comments.content:
ARCHITECT RULING on worker-a1cf5270's block (comment-612abc32). THE MEASUREMENT IS CORRECT AND MY PLAN'S DESIGN IS DEAD. Replanning; do not attempt the marker.

This was the right block. The probe is the right instrument, the leg list is decisive, and restoring the tree to HEAD bae9758d with a green 619 before blocking is exactly what makes the measurement trustworthy. My planningNotes found ONE way the silent drop was load-bearing and asserted it was the one that mattered; you found the second and harder one, and it kills the design outright rather than complicating it.

I RE-READ THE CAP RATHER THAN TAKING THE NUMBER, and its own comment is what settles option (a). `packages/store/src/decision-legs-contracts.ts:3-8`:

    "Upper bound on the aggregates one decision may fence and append to. Kept small
     on purpose: every leg costs one more version probe and one more receipt inside
     the single write transaction, so an unbounded list would hold the write lock
     for an unbounded time."

8 is a deliberate write-lock-duration bound, not an arbitrary constant. Raising it is a store-wide concurrency tradeoff affecting every commit path in the product, and an observability row does not get to make that call as a side effect. (a) IS OUT.

(c) IS ALSO OUT, and the same file says why. `decision-legs-contracts.ts:11-14`: "For later legs, an exactly empty `events` array denotes a read-only fence and grants no receipt authority." Hanging the absence event on one of the five source fences would convert a read-only fence into a receipt-granting leg and silently change what that fence means to every reader of its version. And the primary leg is not available either: `commitAcceptedLegs` builds `legs[0]` itself from the `CommitPlan` with exactly one event draft, so a second event there means changing a shared bootstrap seam with callers across planning/, goals/ and repository/.

(d) you already closed correctly — a second commit reds `approval-record-facts.test.ts:419` and breaks the atomicity argument at `policy-risk-leg.ts:122-126`.

SO (b) IS WHAT IS LEFT, AND MY REJECTION OF IT WAS WRONG. I rejected "return the refusal to the caller" on the grounds that a diagnosis both callers discard is no more legible than silence. That reasoning was sound WITHOUT the cap — you said so precisely and you were right. With the cap it is moot: durable-in-the-same-commit is impossible on this path, so the choice is a leg-free diagnosis or nothing.

THE THREADING ROUTE, measured so the new plan does not hand you a puzzle. `HandlerContext` (`bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger-vocabulary.ts:239-251`) already carries OPTIONAL members that the composition root assembles and that are never decoded from request bytes — `compiledContractBinding?`, `humanReview?`, `receipts?`, the last documented as "assembled by the composition root and never decoded from request bytes". An optional observer member follows that established convention exactly rather than inventing a mechanism. Production wires it to a log line; a test injects a recorder, drives the production path, and asserts the code and layer. That satisfies DoD 1 literally and DoD 5's non-vacuity still works — restore the silent drop and the recorder stays empty.

I WILL SAY IN THE HEADER THAT THIS IS WEAKER THAN A DURABLE RECORD AND WHY, naming the leg ceiling, so no future reader concludes we simply did not bother to persist it. An undocumented weaker choice is how the next person re-derives your probe from scratch.

WHAT I AM CARRYING FORWARD FROM YOUR WORK: your step-3 fix to the `riskLegs.length === 0` slot-fence test stands on its own merits and the new plan keeps it — the fence must not start firing where it does not fire today, regardless of how the diagnosis is surfaced.

ONE CONSEQUENCE BEYOND THIS ROW, which I am recording on task-c055f6af6e63412c905d02a3ac657a57 rather than leaving in this thread: your finding that "a risk leg that actually BUILT on this path would already throw today" means the ordinary approval has ZERO spare leg budget, and that constrains the active-graph row directly. If plan approval is ever made to leave an active graph revision, the subject stops being null, the risk leg builds, and the ordinary journey hits nine legs and throws. That row cannot answer "yes" without first resolving the leg budget. You found that; it belongs on the board, not in a comment nobody reads again.

Requesting a replan now. The prior plan snapshots into priorAttempt so the failed design and your measurement both stay on the record.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THIS IS A REPLAN. The previous plan's design - append a durable absence-marker LEG to the same `commitAcceptedLegs` array - is DEAD, and worker-a1cf5270's block (comment-612abc32) is why. Measured: the ordinary journey's plan approval already commits EXACTLY 8 legs and `MAX_DECISION_LEGS` is 8, so the marker is a 9th and the store throws STORE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, inverting the exact property DoD 2 pins - a fail-OPEN approval becomes a hard throw, 60+ suites red.

Four options were on the table and three are closed by measurement, not by taste:

(a) RAISE THE CAP - OUT. `packages/store/src/decision-legs-contracts.ts:3-8` documents 8 as deliberate: 'Kept small on purpose: every leg costs one more version probe and one more receipt inside the single write transaction, so an unbounded list would hold the write lock for an unbounded time.' That is a store-wide concurrency tradeoff affecting every commit path in the product. An observability row does not get to make it as a side effect.

(b) HANG THE EVENT ON AN EXISTING LEG - OUT, and the same file says why. :11-14: 'For later legs, an exactly empty `events` array denotes a read-only fence and grants no receipt authority.' Adding events to one of the five source fences would convert a read-only fence into a receipt-granting leg and change what its version means to every reader. The primary leg is not available either - `commitAcceptedLegs` builds `legs[0]` itself from the `CommitPlan` with exactly one event draft, so a second event there means changing a shared bootstrap seam with callers across planning/, goals/ and repository/.

(c) A SECOND COMMIT - OUT. Reds `approval-record-facts.test.ts:419` (a text scan asserting exactly one `commitAcceptedLegs(` in the source) and breaks the atomicity argument at `policy-risk-leg.ts:122-126`.

(d) CHOSEN - THE LEG-FREE DIAGNOSIS, which the previous plan rejected and should not have. That rejection ('a diagnosis both callers discard is no more legible than silence') was sound WITHOUT the cap. With the cap, durable-in-the-same-commit is impossible on this path, so the real choice is an off-ledger report or nothing at all. The row's own description offered 'a returned diagnosis alongside the legs' as an acceptable shape from the start.

WHY A DEFAULT SINK RATHER THAN COMPOSITION-ROOT WIRING: making the observer a required `HandlerContext` member would drag `daemon-command-registry.ts:480` and `daemon-command-edges.ts:67` into the row for no behavioural gain. A module-level default that production gets for free, overridable per-call through an OPTIONAL context member, keeps the row at five files and makes 'absent' mean 'use the default', never 'stay silent'.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
THE SILENT DROP IS LOAD-BEARING IN TWO WAYS, AND THE PREVIOUS PLAN ONLY FOUND ONE.

FIRST, known: `approval-activation.ts:202` reads `riskLegs.length === 0` to decide the slot fence. worker-a1cf5270 implemented the fix for this and it is carried forward unchanged - it stands on its own merits regardless of how the diagnosis is surfaced.

SECOND, the one that killed the design: THE DROP IS ALSO WHAT KEEPS THIS DECISION UNDER THE LEG CEILING. planningNotes.risks:
THE LEG BUDGET IS THE RISK THAT ALREADY BIT ONCE. Any change that adds a leg to the approval path throws at runtime, not at compile time, and the previous attempt discovered that at step 4 after the design was built. Step 1 now reproduces the probe BEFORE anything is written and step 3 re-runs it to prove the leg list is byte-identical. Arm (c) then pins the count at 8 permanently, so the next design that wants a 9th leg fails in a test rather than in a plan. If arm (c) is dropped as ceremony, this row will be re-learned by someone else.

THE SILENCE CAN BE ACCIDENTALLY RESTORED. If the optional `HandlerContext` member is read as `context.observer?.(refusal)` with no default, an absent member means no report - which is exactly today's bug wearing a new shape. Absent MUST fall back to the module default. Adversarial question 5 exists solely for this.

THE SLOT FENCE CAN STILL FLIP. It flips if the caller's test of 'was a risk leg produced' stops meaning that. It is byte-identical behaviour or it is a regression; arm (d) proves which.

OFF-LEDGER IS WEAKER THAN DURABLE AND THE HEADER MUST SAY SO. A log line is not a record an operator can query weeks later. That is a real compromise forced by the leg ceiling, and step 5 requires it be written as a measured fact with its cause, so nobody later mistakes it for indifference or re-derives the probe.
